title: Deciding Whether Our Niece Is Ready for Social Media
script: Ayu: [thoughtful] Bram, Sari's been asking our brother for an account on that app all her classmates use, and he's asked us what we honestly think.
Bram: Thirteen feels young to me, though I'm aware that argument alone won't get us very far, given how normal it's become at that age.
Ayu: [carefully] It's not really about age in isolation, is it? It's whether she's equipped to handle comparing her ordinary life to everyone else's carefully edited highlights.
Bram: True. At that age, I imagine every filtered photo would have felt like undeniable proof that everyone else's life was simply better than mine.
Ayu: [reflective] Exactly what worries me. Adults struggle with that comparison trap, and we've had decades to build up some resistance to it.
Bram: Should we just tell him to refuse outright, then? Or would that risk making the whole thing more tempting, something she'll pursue secretly instead?
Ayu: [honestly] That's the real dilemma, isn't it. Forbidding it entirely rarely eliminates the desire; it just removes any chance of guiding her through it.
Bram: Maybe a private account then, visible only to people she actually knows, with him following along rather than snooping from a distance.
Ayu: [gently] I like that better than an outright ban. It teaches her to navigate it with support, instead of either total exposure or total prohibition.
Bram: We should probably suggest he talk with her directly too, about what's real versus staged, before she starts scrolling unsupervised.
Ayu: [calmly] Absolutely. If she understands early that a photo represents someone's best five seconds, not their entire existence, that alone might soften the comparison.
Bram: Should we mention what happened to our cousin's daughter, the one who deleted everything after feeling awful for months?
Ayu: [encouraging] Perhaps, though carefully. We want him informed, not so alarmed that he swings to the opposite extreme and bans it in a panic.
Bram: Fair point. Let's write down a few concrete suggestions rather than just voicing worries, since worries alone rarely help anyone decide anything.
Ayu: [seriously] Agreed. We'll call him this weekend, present it calmly, and trust that he'll make the right call for his own daughter.

quiz.question: Why has their brother asked Ayu and Bram for their opinion?
options: He wants to buy Sari a phone
Sari broke a rule already
Sari has been asking for a social media account and he wants their honest opinion
He is moving to a new city
quiz.explanation: Sari has been asking for an account on the app her classmates use, and their brother asked what they think.

quiz.question: What does Ayu say the real concern is, beyond age alone?
options: The cost of the app
Whether Sari is equipped to handle comparing her ordinary life to others' edited highlights
Whether the app is popular enough
Whether Sari has enough friends already
quiz.explanation: Ayu says it's not just about age, but whether Sari can handle comparing her life to everyone else's edited highlights.

quiz.question: What risk does Bram raise about simply forbidding the account outright?
options: It might make Sari angry at them specifically
It would cost extra money
It would upset their brother
It could make the whole thing more tempting and lead her to pursue it secretly
quiz.explanation: Bram worries an outright refusal might make it more tempting, something she pursues secretly instead.

quiz.question: What compromise do Ayu and Bram settle on?
options: A public account with no restrictions
No account until she turns eighteen
A private account visible only to people she knows, with her father following along
An account managed entirely by her father
quiz.explanation: They suggest a private account visible only to people she actually knows, with her father following along rather than snooping.

quiz.question: What do they decide to do instead of just voicing worries to their brother?
options: Write down a few concrete suggestions to present calmly
Say nothing at all
Tell their brother he must ban the app
Ask Sari directly to decide for herself
quiz.explanation: They decide to write down concrete suggestions rather than just voicing worries, and present it calmly this weekend.

quiz.question: Why is age alone an incomplete measure of Sari's readiness?
options: Last week, my phone rang from an unfamiliar number
Our caller has strong feelings on this
Whether facial recognition was necessary for attendance at all.
Her ability to handle comparison and edited images matters more.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Her ability to handle comparison and edited images matters more.

quiz.question: What risk could an absolute social-media ban create?
options: She might use the platform secretly without adult guidance.
He claimed he'd been in an accident, that his phone was damaged
That's a sobering way to reach clarity
They learned their options, storage period, and review route.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: She might use the platform secretly without adult guidance.

quiz.question: Which compromise balances supervision with some independence?
options: What disturbs me most isn't the technology itself
Use a private account with supportive parental involvement.
A few assumed I'd become less committed, which stung initially
Her case was not campaign material without her consent.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Use a private account with supportive parental involvement.

quiz.question: What should her father explain about attractive online images?
options: They show selected moments rather than a person's whole life.
It feels almost absurd, verifying my own brother like he's a stranger at the door
A shared rule protects those who'd never dare raise the issue alone
A machine's output carried more authority than a student's account.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: They show selected moments rather than a person's whole life.

quiz.question: Why do Ayu and Bram prepare concrete suggestions before calling?
options: My brother, for his part, finds the whole ordeal hilarious
Specific safeguards will help more than fear-based warnings.
I hope someone finally silences their notifications after we finish talking tonight
Human review, limited data, and accessible correction must be built in.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Specific safeguards will help more than fear-based warnings.
